facts.statement: The genus Aegyptosaurus was described by German paleontologist Ernst Stromer in 1932.
facts.quote: Aegyptosaurus was described by German paleontologist Ernst Stromer in 1932

facts.statement: Most original specimens of Aegyptosaurus were destroyed in an Allied bombing raid on the Munich museum on April 25, 1944.
facts.quote: All of the specimens destroyed in 1944 were discovered before 1939 and the fossils were stored together in Munich, but were obliterated when an Allied bombing raid destroyed the museum where they were kept on 25 April 1944, during World War II

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Aegyptosaurus to be 15 meters long and weigh 7 tonnes based on comparisons with Paralititan.
facts.quote: In 2010, based on Paralititan and other related titanosaurs, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Aegyptosaurus at 15 m, and its weight at 7 tonnes

facts.statement: Aegyptosaurus was a quadrupedal dinosaur with a long neck and tail and a small skull.
facts.quote: Aegyptosaurus era un dinosaurio de cuello y cola largos, cráneo pequeño y de cuatro patas

facts.statement: Paul estimated that this large herbivore stood 5 meters tall in addition to being 15 meters long and weighing 7 tonnes.
facts.quote: Basándose en Paralititan Paul estimó que este gran herbívoro medía 15 metros de longitud y 5 de altura y un peso de 7 toneladas

facts.statement: The holotype of Aegyptosaurus consists of three caudal vertebrae, a partial scapula, and nine limb bones.
facts.quote: Aegyptosaurus se basa en el holotipo, '1912VIII61, un espécimen que consiste en 3 vértebras caudales, un omóplato parcial, y 9 huesos de los miembros

facts.statement: Aegyptosaurus lived in Africa during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 95 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 95 millones de años, en el Cenomaniense, en África

facts.statement: Aegyptosaurus is the only known species of the extinct genus, classified as a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: es la única especie conocida del género extinto Aegyptosaurus de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosauriano

facts.statement: Fossils of Aegyptosaurus have been found in the Bahariya Formation in Egypt and the Farak Formation in Niger.
facts.quote: Encontrados en la Formación Baharija en Marsá Matrú, Agadez en Egipto y en la Formación Farak en Tahoua, Níger, ambos lugares en África del Norte

facts.statement: Aegyptosaurus shared its habitat and time period with large predators such as Carcharodontosaurus and Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Los egiptosaurios compartieron el lugar y edad con grandes cazadores como Carcharodontosaurus y Spinosaurus

facts.statement: Aegyptosaurus belongs to the parent group Titanosauria.
The time range for Aegyptosaurus is estimated from the Berriasian to the Cenomanian, between 143.1 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Cenomanian (143.1 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Aegyptosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur discovered in Egypt.
rejected.quote: Aegyptosaurus (meaning 'Egypt's lizard') is a genus of sauropod dinosaur discovered in Egypt
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is a genus of sauropod dinosaur discovered in'

rejected.statement: Aegyptosaurus lived in what is now Africa around 95 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous Period.
rejected.quote: that lived in what is now Africa, around 95 million years ago, during the Late Cretaceous Period (Cenomanian faunal stage)
